issue.title: build(go-dist): admit lang-go into canonical native payloads and attest actual compiler features

repository.name: ripr-swarm
repository.description: Swarm development lane for ripr: static RIPR evidence for CI, editors, and agents.

issue.body:
Parent/controller: #5519 under #5518 and #5774.
Depends on: #6225; accepted `lang-go` feature identity from #5535; parser/dependency disposition from #5534; final-payload authority #4521.

## Outcome

Build an explicitly Go-capable native ripr payload through the canonical release path and prove from actual compiler artifacts and staged bytes that `lang-go` is present. This is release-payload admission, not Cargo-default promotion or Go support adjudication.

## Current boundary

At `ripr-swarm/main` `8f29e0cfefe77488136ea1e3cf3ac4e269ca636b`, native release policy and the release-server producer select only `lang-python`, `lang-rust`, and `lang-typescript`. #5535 deliberately introduces `lang-go` as non-default first. #6225 must make that selection representable without lying about ordinary `cargo install ripr`.

## One-PR scope

- Select `lang-go` in the canonical native release-build contract for an explicitly scoped Go-capable preview candidate.
- Drive the real Cargo invocation from that typed selection; no hand-maintained parallel argument list.
- Extend release-server producer/payload DTOs and rendered receipts so the effective feature set, build arguments, Cargo artifact identity, executable hash, parser/helper prerequisites, target and staged payload digest are bound together.
- Consume the final native payload created by #4521; do not create a Go-specific staging directory or archive builder.
- If the accepted parser introduces generated C/build-script artifacts, record their dependency/license/toolchain implications through existing policy and receipts. If the accepted architecture needs a runtime helper, bind its version, target, schema, digest, relative layout and compatibility rather than assuming one.
- Preserve existing archive shape and server/editor consumers unless the accepted payload genuinely adds a required file; any layout change is explicit and versioned.
- Keep Go runtime activation/config and preview support semantics owned by #5535/#5556.

## Required falsifiers

1. Same product/version built without `lang-go`, with a valid `ripr --version`, is rejected.
2. Desired metadata says `lang-go` but actual compiler artifacts omit it -> reject.
3. Compiler artifacts include an unrecorded extra feature -> reject.
4. Staged executable is replaced after feature attestation -> reject by digest/currentness.
5. Wrong target, stale Cargo.lock, moved source tree, parser/helper version drift or payload-layout substitution -> reject.
6. Go-capable payload is tested with Go explicitly disabled -> reports disabled, not unavailable or silently enabled.
7. Binary built without `lang-go` and explicit Go config -> reports the existing typed unavailable-feature recovery.
8. Existing three-language payload still qualifies under its own exact contract and cannot inherit the Go claim.

## Acceptance

- [ ] one real exact-candidate native build records `lang-go` in actual compiler-artifact and final-payload evidence;
- [ ] the staged executable/payload bytes match the recorded digests and effective feature contract;
- [ ] all required parser/helper/runtime prerequisites are in the payload contract or explicitly absent;
- [ ] same-version Go-less and post-stage replacement controls fail the production verifier;
- [ ] selected target counts are nonzero and missing/unsupported rows cannot render as pass;
- [ ] current archive extraction/version/checksum/server-manifest behavior remains green;
- [ ] `cargo xtask check-release-targets`, focused release-server/payload tests, policy/license/generated checks and exact-candidate archive qualification pass;
- [ ] no public copy or metadata claims ordinary Cargo installation contains Go.

## Proof

Retain the exact source SHA/tree, Cargo.lock digest, toolchain, Cargo arguments, compiler artifact, effective feature set, final payload DTO/digest, archive digest, executed target rows and negative-control outputs. A desired manifest plus a successful build is insufficient without reading and comparing the actual artifact/payload identity.

## Non-goals

No Cargo default-feature change, wheel/npm adapter build, installed consumer journey, Go analyzer implementation, support-tier decision, registry publication, tag/release, settings/secret change or automatic release membership.

## Claim boundary

Completion proves the canonical native payload was built with the accepted Go feature and exact prerequisites. It does not prove installed Go behavior, ordinary Cargo-install availability, semantic quality, or public delivery.

issue.title: build(go-dist): bind wheel and npm native builds to the canonical Go feature receipt

repository.name: ripr-swarm
repository.description: Swarm development lane for ripr: static RIPR evidence for CI, editors, and agents.

issue.body:
Parent/controller: #5519 under #5518 and #5774.
Depends on: #6225, #6227, wheel owner #4490, npm owner #4491, final-payload identity #4521.

## Problem

The Python wheel authoring file currently hardcodes `lang-python`, `lang-rust`, and `lang-typescript`, while npm native payload production has its own package-generation path. Once `lang-go` is selected for a release, independently editing those adapters would allow archive, wheel, and npm packages with the same product version to contain different compiled capabilities.

Source-manifest parity is not sufficient: Maturin repair/strip and npm payload staging can transform or substitute container contents after a desired feature list was written.

## One-PR outcome

Make the wheel and npm native package builders consume and attest the exact canonical selected-feature/final-payload identity rather than restating it.

## Required behavior

- Drive Maturin's effective feature arguments from the #6225 distribution-build contract. Generated authoring may materialize a checked list, but drift must fail before packaging.
- Drive each npm native payload package from the same selected final payload or prove byte/digest equivalence through #4521/#4624. The CommonJS launcher remains a launcher; it does not compile features.
- Bind package/container receipts to source SHA/tree, native version, target, Cargo.lock, selected/effective features, final payload aggregate digest, package digest and any post-build repair/strip transformation.
- Validate that every selected adapter package exposes the same product capability generation for the same target/version.
- Keep target availability independent: a selected platform subset is allowed when manifests, optional dependencies and public copy cannot imply absent payload packages exist.
- Preserve wheel `bindings = "bin"`, no-sdist posture, npm exact optional-dependency policy and scripts-disabled installation.

## Falsifiers

1. Native archive contains Go but wheel is built with the old three-feature list -> fail.
2. Wheel contains Go but one npm native package uses a Go-less payload -> fail.
3. Same target/version points to a different final payload digest -> fail.
4. Maturin or npm staging substitutes the executable after payload admission -> fail.
5. Launcher optional dependencies use ranges or a mismatched version -> fail.
6. Package metadata claims a full target matrix while only a subset exists -> fail.
7. Container hash changes while extracted admitted payload identity remains the same -> record the transformation; do not falsely require container-byte equality.
8. A package falls back to compiling, downloading or finding an ambient ripr at install/runtime -> fail.

## Acceptance

- [ ] wheel and npm package builds consume one typed selected-feature/final-payload authority;
- [ ] same-target extracted payload identity agrees with the canonical archive through #4624;
- [ ] actual packaged executable features include `lang-go` when the selected release contract does;
- [ ] package receipts distinguish final payload digest from wheel/tarball/container digest;
- [ ] wrong-feature, wrong-target, substituted-payload and mismatched-version controls fail production checks;
- [ ] current package contents allowlists, licenses, RECORD/npm files, permissions and scripts-disabled behavior remain valid;
- [ ] `cargo xtask check-release-targets`, package authoring/unit tests, Maturin/npm dry-run checks, payload parity checks and file/generated policy pass.

## Non-goals

No installed Go semantic journey, registry publication, account/publisher setup, new package names, Cargo default change, package-manager channel, analyzer work or support promotion.

## Claim boundary

Completion proves wheel and npm native package builders package the same Go-selected native product identity as the canonical archive. It does not prove those packages install or analyze Go correctly on a clean consumer; that belongs to #5521 children.

issue.title: build(go-dist): apply the accepted ordinary Cargo-install and default-feature ruling

repository.name: ripr-swarm
repository.description: Swarm development lane for ripr: static RIPR evidence for CI, editors, and agents.

issue.body:
Parent/controller: #5519 under #5518 and #5774.
Blocked on: support/default/activation adjudication #5556; distribution contract #6225; Go-capable native payload #6227; installed Go evidence from #5521 children.

## Outcome

Apply the exact #5556 ruling for ordinary `cargo install ripr` and Cargo default features, then prove the published crate behavior matches the claim. This issue exists so preview payload selection cannot silently become a default-feature decision inside #6227.

The terminal outcome may be either:

```text
A. lang-go becomes a Cargo default and ordinary cargo install is Go-capable
B. lang-go remains non-default and ordinary cargo install makes no Go claim
```

A no-change ruling is valid only with a checked, public non-claim and an exact supported explicit-install route where one is offered.

## Required work

### If Go becomes a default

- Add `lang-go` to `[features].default` and the ordinary-install feature contract from #6225.
- Update crate/package/release checks that bind default features.
- Build the actual packaged crate, install it in an isolated Cargo root with the supported Cargo/Rust toolchain, remove source-checkout and ambient ripr access, and run the installed Go fixture.
- Preserve existing Rust/Python/TypeScript defaults and explicit language configuration authority.

### If Go remains non-default

- Keep `[features].default` unchanged.
- Ensure package metadata, README, installer output and doctor/support surfaces do not imply `cargo install ripr` provides Go.
- If an explicit source-install command is supported, make it exact and mechanically verified, for example through the accepted equivalent of `cargo install ripr --features lang-go`; do not invent it before the published crate actually supports it.
- Make absence distinguishable from Go disabled in project configuration.

## Required controls

1. Packaged-crate install, not `cargo install --path`, is the consumer subject.
2. Default-claimed build without `lang-go` fails the installed Go journey even if version matches.
3. Non-default ruling plus Go metadata/README claim fails product-copy/package checks.
4. Explicit-feature install with misspelled/unavailable feature fails visibly.
5. Custom Rust-only build reports Go unavailable; an explicitly disabled project reports disabled.
6. Existing default-language behavior and source package contents remain valid.
7. `cargo install --locked` and ordinary documented install semantics are distinguished where the lockfile contract differs.
8. Published MSRV/build prerequisites remain separate from prerequisites for analyzing a Go repository.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Cargo default features and the ordinary-install contract match the terminal #5556 ruling;
- [ ] the actual packaged crate is installed and exercised outside the source checkout;
- [ ] when Go is claimed, the installed binary produces nonzero accepted Go evidence and a working continuation command;
- [ ] when Go is not claimed, package copy and diagnostics state the exact explicit route or non-availability without ambiguity;
- [ ] same-version Go-less, ambient-binary and source-path substitution controls fail;
- [ ] crate packaging, public API, version, release-target, package quickstart and installed-journey checks pass;
- [ ] exact Cargo/Rust versions, crate archive digest, installed executable digest, selected features, fixture subjects and cleanup are retained.

## Non-goals

No support ruling inside this issue, no native archive/wheel/npm feature selection, no registry publication, no Go analyzer change, no automatic runtime enablement, and no promise that every package manager shares Cargo's build prerequisites.

## Claim boundary

Completion makes ordinary Cargo installation tell the truth about Go according to the accepted support decision. It does not publish the crate or establish other channels/platforms.

repository.name: ripr-swarm
repository.description: Swarm development lane for ripr: static RIPR evidence for CI, editors, and agents.

issue.body:
Parent: #5518. Canonical programme controller: #5774.
This issue is the **payload/build controller**. Implementation belongs to the focused children below; do not open a single PR claiming all of #5519.

## Outcome

Every Go-advertised ripr artifact is built from one exact selected feature/prerequisite contract, carries the canonical final native payload identity, and tells the truth about ordinary Cargo installation. Compiled availability, project activation and support tier remain independently governed.

Observed baseline when decomposed: `ripr-swarm/main` `8f29e0cfefe77488136ea1e3cf3ac4e269ca636b`. Cargo defaults, `policy/distribution.toml`, Maturin and release-server policy still select only `lang-python`, `lang-rust` and `lang-typescript`. The distribution schema structurally equates selected release features with Cargo defaults; Go has not been admitted prematurely.

## Child graph

```text
#6225 architecture(distribution)
  separate Cargo defaults / ordinary install / selected release features

#6225 + #5534 + #5535 + #4521
  -> #6227 build(go-dist)
     admit lang-go into canonical native payloads and attest actual compiler features

#6225 + #6227 + #4490 + #4491 + #4521
  -> #6229 build(go-dist)
     bind wheel and npm native builds to the canonical Go feature/payload receipt

#5556 + #6225 + #6227 + installed evidence
  -> #6230 build(go-dist)
     apply the accepted ordinary Cargo-install/default-feature ruling
```

The children are independently reviewable:

| Child | Owns | Does not own |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #6225 | Generic typed feature-selection architecture and schema migration | Any Go selection |
| #6227 | Exact Go-selected native release payload and actual compiler/payload attestation | Cargo default promotion, wheel/npm install, support tier |
| #6229 | Wheel/npm builders consuming the canonical selected payload/feature authority | Installed journeys or publication |
| #6230 | Final ordinary Cargo-install/default-feature behavior after #5556 | The support ruling itself or other channels |

Shared owners remain authoritative: #4488 package identity/version/targets, #4521 final payload identity, #4490 wheels, #4491 npm, #4621/#4622/#4623 native compatibility. Extend them; do not create a Go-specific release framework.

## Dependency law

- #5534 decides parser/dependency architecture; packaging records the accepted result rather than choosing it.
- #5535 establishes the `lang-go` feature/availability identity initially without forcing default promotion.
- A non-publishing explicitly selected preview payload may be built through #6227 to obtain installed evidence before #5556.
- If #5556 later changes Cargo defaults or selected payload bytes, #6230 applies the ruling and all affected installed evidence is requalified.
- A package install never overrides explicit `[languages].enabled` configuration.
- A runtime helper is included only if the accepted analyzer architecture genuinely requires one; its version/schema/target/digest/layout become part of the same final payload identity.

## Cross-child falsifiers

The controller cannot close while any advertised artifact can pass under one of these conditions:

- desired metadata says Go but compiler artifacts omit `lang-go`;
- archive, wheel and npm packages for the same selected target/version contain divergent ungoverned payloads;
- a same-version Go-less executable inherits Go qualification from `--version`;
- Cargo defaults are changed implicitly inside preview payload work;
- an ordinary Cargo install is described as Go-capable when #6230/#5556 say otherwise;
- unknown extra features, stale parser/helper inputs, wrong target, moved lock/source tree or post-stage substitution are accepted;
- package target subsets masquerade as the full matrix.

## Controller acceptance

- [ ] #6225 is accepted and one typed authority distinguishes crate availability, Cargo defaults, selected release build and effective features;
- [ ] #6227 proves actual compiler-artifact and final-payload Go selection with a same-version Go-less negative;
- [ ] #6229 binds wheel/npm package production to the same selected identity and passes same-target parity controls;
- [ ] #6230 records and proves the terminal ordinary Cargo-install/default ruling from #5556;
- [ ] exact parser/helper/runtime prerequisites, target, source/tree, lockfile, toolchain and payload digests are retained;
- [ ] existing languages, version bump, archive/editor consumers, license/file/generated policy and compatibility owners remain green;
- [ ] no child claims installed semantic usefulness, support tier or public state beyond its own evidence.

## Invalidation

A parser/helper architecture, Cargo feature, build-argument, lockfile, source tree, target, payload layout or staged-byte change invalidates dependent #6227/#6229 evidence. A #5556 default/support ruling that changes bytes or ordinary-install behavior invalidates affected installed and documentation evidence; do not edit old receipt fields in place.

## Non-goals

No Go parser/classifier implementation, installed consumer journey, support adjudication, package publication, tag/release, credentials/settings, external package-manager submission or automatic release membership.

## Claim boundary

Closing #5519 means the complete selected build/payload/Cargo-default graph is terminal and internally consistent. It does not prove installed Go behavior or authorize public delivery.

issue.title: epic(go-distribution): deliver discoverable Go-capable ripr installs through the existing product channels

repository.name: ripr-swarm
repository.description: Swarm development lane for ripr: static RIPR evidence for CI, editors, and agents.

issue.body:
## Outcome

A Go developer can discover ripr, install an exact selected release without obtaining a Rust toolchain on native channels, analyze a real Go change, understand the result or named limitation, and follow the supported next command. Product/executable/Cargo identity stays `ripr`; PyPI stays `ripr-rs`; npm stays `@effortlessmetrics/ripr`.

This is the distribution/installed-use/discovery programme under canonical Go controller #5774. It consumes Go analyzer authority #5520 and shared semantic contracts; it does not implement a second parser, classifier, output model, editor or release framework.

No release version, source integration, publication, tag, signing, credential/settings action, repository creation, external listing submission or support promotion is authorized by this issue.

## Verified baseline when decomposed — 2026-10-04

Inspected `ripr-swarm/main` `8f29e0cfefe77488136ea1e3cf3ac4e269ca636b`:

- Cargo defaults, `policy/distribution.toml`, Maturin and release-server policy still select `lang-python`, `lang-rust`, `lang-typescript`; Go has not leaked into release bytes.
- Distribution schema 1.0 equates release-selected features with Cargo defaults. #6225 owns the required generic split.
- #4488 package identity/version/target authority and #4521 final native payload identity are landed.
- #4490/#4491/#4492/#4493 remain the shared wheel/npm/installed/no-publish implementation owners.
- #4621/#4622/#4623 own native compatibility; #4624 parity, #4628 installed stdio, #4630 typed receipts and #4633 CI routing are shared extension points.
- #5236 native generated-workflow installer is merged for Linux/macOS; Windows x64 ZIP remains #6245.
- #5284 cargo-binstall metadata/install-channel preparation is merged; public readback belongs to source verification.
- Go implementation remains #5520 with spec/parser/scaffold/fixtures/output/editor/corpus/support owners #5533–#5556 plus #5758/#5761/#5765.

## Governing decisions

1. **No placeholder Go module.** The Rust CLI does not acquire a `go install`/pkg.go.dev identity merely because it analyzes Go. Durable decision owner: [ripr #1822](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr/issues/1822).
2. **Compiled availability, ordinary Cargo defaults, project activation and support tier are independent.** #6225 represents them; #5556 rules on them; #6230 applies the ordinary Cargo decision.
3. **Existing package identities remain canonical.** No `ripr-go`, unscoped npm alias, PyPI `ripr`, Python import SDK or JavaScript SDK.
4. **Shared owners are extended, not cloned.** Go-specific fixtures/receipts feed #4490–#4493/#4624/#4628/#4630/#4633.
5. **Channels and targets are admitted independently.** A bounded preview may ship through a selected subset. Omitted rows remain explicit and cannot masquerade as a full matrix.
6. **No automatic release membership.** Version/candidate/source transaction remains with the existing release controllers.

# Execution graph

## A. Build and payload contract — controller #5519

```text
#6225 separate Cargo defaults from selected release features
  -> #6227 admit lang-go into canonical native payloads
  -> #6229 bind wheel/npm builders to canonical feature/payload identity

#5556 + installed evidence
  -> #6230 apply ordinary Cargo-install/default ruling
```

#6227 can build a non-publishing explicitly selected preview candidate to obtain evidence without forcing Cargo defaults. Any later byte-changing ruling requires successor qualification.

## B. Installed-use qualification — controller #5521

```text
#6231 common digest-bound installed Go fixture/answer key
  -> #6233 canonical archive journey
  -> #6234 ripr-rs wheel journey
  -> #6237 scoped npm package journey

#6233 + #6234 + #6237 + shared parity/stdio rows
  -> #6238 typed Go capability receipt and aggregate gate
```

Cargo source-install proof is #6230 after #5556. #4624/#4628/#4633 remain shared parity/protocol/routing owners. Same-version Go-less, disabled, unavailable, zero-subject, ambient, wrong-target and stale-artifact states must remain distinct.

## C. Package discovery and first-use docs — controller #5544

```text
selected payload/package identity
  -> #6240 truthful Cargo/PyPI/npm built-artifact metadata

#6240 + #5556 + installed journeys
  -> #6243 executed version-specific install-to-first-Go-result quickstarts
```

Generic snippet architecture remains #4629. Historical/Go-less versions cannot inherit future copy.

## D. Generated CI — controller #5548

```text
#5236 + #4623
  -> #6245 canonical Windows x64 ZIP installer route

#6231 + #6233 + #6238 + #5552 + selected installer rows
  -> #6246 execute real generated Go workflow against exact local assets
```

Native installation and Go semantic output are different proofs. Advisory policy may stay non-blocking; incomplete/disabled/failed Go analysis cannot look clean.

## E. Editor and native package-manager consumers

- #5553 owns Go LSP/editor activation, selectors, menu surfaces and packaged-VSIX/server proof. It consumes #6227/#6233 rather than building a second server.
- #5379 Homebrew, #5557 aqua, #5558 WinGet and #5561 Scoop consume canonical source-release assets and independently prove their selected targets. None is a universal first-preview blocker.
- cargo-binstall consumes the public GitHub release assets; its public journey is verified downstream rather than implemented again.

## F. Support adjudication

#5556 consumes analyzer calibration plus exact distribution evidence:

```text
#5555 judged Go corpus
+ #6227 payload availability
+ #6233/#6234/#6237 installed behavior
+ #6238 aggregate Go capability gate
+ applicable #5552/#5553/#6246/channel evidence
  -> independent rulings for defaults, activation, support, enrichment and matrix
```

A default-feature decision does not imply auto-activation. A preview tier does not excuse zero-subject execution. A supported platform does not imply every package manager.

## G. Source-owned release and public proof

Source controller: [ripr #1816](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr/issues/1816).

```text
selected integrated source + accepted swarm evidence
  -> ripr#1819 exact channel-admission packet
  -> separately authorized existing per-channel publication owners
  -> ripr#1820 independent public install/readback/Go journey verification
```

Publication is source-owned. Swarm readiness does not grant registry, tag, marketplace, tap/bucket or secret authority.

## H. Discovery after public proof

Source controller: [ripr #1817](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr/issues/1817).

```text
ripr#1822 durable no-placeholder-module decision          [can land before release]
ripr#1820 public verified evidence
  -> ripr#1821 analysis-tools.dev / Go Wiki candidate packets
  -> ripr#1823 GitHub repository metadata desired-state packet
```

Preparation is not submission/application. External acceptance and repository settings remain separately authorized.

# Minimum useful preview path

```text
accepted Go semantics/fixture
-> #6225
-> #6227
-> #6231
-> #6233
-> #6238
-> #5556
-> #6230/#6240/#6243 as selected
-> ripr#1819
-> authorized publication
-> ripr#1820
```

Wheel/npm/editor/generated-CI/native-manager branches join only when selected. #6229/#6234/#6237 are required for wheel/npm claims; #5553 for editor; #6245/#6246 for generated CI/Windows; native-manager leaves for their channels.

# Invalidation law

- Parser/helper/source-span/capability changes invalidate dependent fixture, payload, installed and support evidence.
- Cargo feature/build-argument/lock/source/target/payload movement invalidates #6227/#6229 and downstream packages.
- Fixture/config/activation/output changes invalidate #6231 journeys and #6238.
- Support/default/activation changes invalidate #6230/#6240/#6243 and any public packet bound to the old ruling.
- Integrated source or rebuilt artifact movement invalidates source admission/public evidence.
- Public package bytes/tags are immutable; correction uses existing channel fix-forward.

# Programme acceptance

- [ ] Every selected build/payload child under #5519 is terminal and internally consistent.
- [ ] Every selected installed channel/target has nonzero Go behavior evidence or explicit omission/deferment under #5521.
- [ ] #6238 rejects Go-less, disabled, zero-subject, missing, stale, substituted and skipped required rows.
- [ ] Package metadata and quickstarts under #5544 match exact selected versions/support/platforms and executed commands.
- [ ] Generated CI/editor/native-manager claims are independently proved rather than inherited.
- [ ] #5556 records separate default, activation, tier, enrichment and channel/target rulings.
- [ ] Source rollout distinguishes prepared, authorized, published and publicly verified states through #1819/#1820.
- [ ] Discovery preparation/acceptance/settings states remain distinct through #1821/#1822/#1823.
- [ ] No rival package identity, Go module, installer framework, receipt schema or release authority survives.

## Non-goals and action boundary

No code, build, PR dispatch, candidate selection, merge, source sync, release, publication, credentials, repository settings, tap/bucket creation or external submission is authorized by this epic. Work is accepted per focused child, not by issue count or green generic CI.

## Claim boundary

Closing #5518 proves the selected Go distribution graph was implemented, qualified, adjudicated, publicly delivered and independently verified through its explicit rows. It does not establish universal Go accuracy, every platform or every package manager.

issue.title: support(go): adjudicate Go preview support after analyzer and distribution proof

repository.name: ripr-swarm
repository.description: Swarm development lane for ripr: static RIPR evidence for CI, editors, and agents.

issue.body:
Parent: #5520. Canonical programme controller: #5774.
Distribution/install companion: #5518.
Analyzer calibration owner: #5555.

## Outcome

Make the exact evidence-backed rulings about what ripr may publicly claim for Go after analyzer and installed-artifact evidence exists. Keep compiled payload selection, ordinary Cargo defaults, project activation, support tier, enrichment and channel/surface matrices independent.

This is an adjudication issue. It implements no parser, analyzer, package, installer, metadata, workflow or publication behavior. Downstream issues apply its rulings.

# Required evidence generations

## Analyzer/product inputs

Consume the exact accepted generation from #5520/#5774, including:

- #5533 behavior contract and #5534 parser decision;
- #5535 availability/config scaffold and #5536 conformance fixture authority;
- project/package/binding/owner/test/activation/oracle/relation/limit producers (#5537–#5551, #5758, #5761);
- #5765 repository/mixed-repo completeness status;
- #5552 CLI/JSON/SARIF/agent/MCP parity;
- #5553 editor/LSP evidence where an editor claim is considered;
- #5555 governed judged corpus with false-actionable, false-exposed, conservative under-credit, correct limitation and inconclusive denominators;
- #5554/#5549 explicit optional/deferred disposition when enrichment or third-party assertions are named.

## Distribution/installed inputs

Use focused distribution owners rather than broad umbrella status:

- #6227 actual `lang-go`-selected canonical native payload and compiler-artifact evidence;
- #6233 native archive installed Go journey as the minimum prebuilt baseline;
- #6234 wheel and #6237 npm journeys only when those channels are considered;
- #6238 exact Go capability rows/aggregate package gate;
- #4624 payload parity and #4628 installed stdio rows where claimed;
- #6246 generated-CI evidence where CI is considered;
- #5553 packaged editor/server evidence where editor delivery is considered;
- #5379/#5557/#5558/#5561 only for native package-manager rows actually considered.

#6225 represents release selection versus Cargo defaults. #6230 applies the Cargo-default ruling **after** this issue; #6240/#6243 apply final package copy and commands. Do not require those downstream implementations as evidence for deciding their governing state.

## Evidence admission law

- Every input binds exact source/tree, parser/capability generation, configuration, fixture/corpus, selected feature/payload and installed artifact identities.
- Missing, stale, skipped, zero-subject, wrong-version, ambient, substituted or unsupported-required evidence is not pass.
- A same-version Go-less executable cannot support any Go-capable channel row even when package/version checks pass.
- Explicit Go disabled, feature unavailable, analysis limited and analysis failed remain distinct.
- One target/channel/surface cannot donate evidence to another.
- Preview is a support label, not permission for fabricated completion. A preview row still requires honest nonzero execution or a named limitation.
- Static evidence and runtime `go test`/mutation evidence remain separate axes.

# Independent rulings

Record each item separately with decision, evidence, deciding criterion, non-claims and what would change the ruling.

## 1. Release-payload compiled availability

Does the selected native release payload contain `lang-go`? This can be yes for an explicitly selected preview payload without deciding Cargo defaults.

## 2. Ordinary Cargo-install/default features

Does ordinary `cargo install ripr` contain Go, or is an explicit feature route/no-claim retained? Hand off the terminal ruling to #6230.

## 3. Runtime project activation

Choose among explicit configuration only, bounded no-config auto-detection, or another accepted policy. Explicit `[languages].enabled` remains authoritative. Default compilation never silently implies auto-activation.

## 4. Support tier

Preview/advisory is the expected first candidate. Any stronger tier requires evidence at that level. State whether findings, limitations, repair routes, repository mode and editor/CI surfaces have different tiers.

## 5. Toolchain enrichment

For each named capability, rule `unavailable`, `optional`, or `required`. Syntax-first analysis must not acquire a hidden Go-toolchain/network/module-download prerequisite.

## 6. Semantic scope and non-claims

Name accepted Go versions/syntax, module/workspace/build-context handling, test shapes, oracle families, relations, repository mode and high-frequency typed unknowns. Interfaces, cgo/assembly, generated/vendor files, dynamic helpers/frameworks and other boundaries stay local and explicit.

## 7. Platform/channel matrix

List only archive/Cargo/wheel/npm/editor/CI/native-manager target combinations with retained exact installed proof. A platform claim does not imply every package manager, and a package-manager claim does not imply every target.

## 8. Public surface matrix

Rule independently on CLI, JSON/SARIF, agent/MCP, LSP/editor, generated CI and package-manager quickstarts. Omitted/deferred surfaces remain omitted rather than inheriting core CLI support.

# Support packet

Produce one versioned machine-readable packet plus human projection binding:

```text
source/candidate/parser/capability generation
feature selection and Cargo-default decision inputs
activation/config policy
support tier per semantic/surface mode
Go/test/oracle/package/build-context scope
known limitations/non-claims
toolchain enrichment policy
judged-corpus rows/denominators/verdicts
installed package/channel/target evidence identities
selected platform/channel/surface matrix
downstream implementation obligations
invalidation conditions
```

Counts derive from rows. Missing detail or unsupported states remain explicit; no prose-only green summary.

# Required controls

1. Same-version Go-less artifact is substituted -> compiled/channel rows reject.
2. Explicit-disabled fixture is treated as unavailable or supported execution -> reject state collapse.
3. Zero analyzed Go subjects or missing corpus denominator -> hold.
4. False-exposed and false-actionable are combined into a favorable average -> reject packet.
5. One Linux archive row is generalized to macOS/Windows/wheel/npm/editor/CI -> reject matrix.
6. Default-feature yes is copied into auto-activation yes -> reject independent-ruling parity.
7. Optional `go list` evidence is used to claim syntax-first requires a Go toolchain -> reject prerequisite drift.
8. Package metadata/README wording outruns the packet -> downstream copy gate fails.
9. Material parser/binding/oracle/payload/config movement reuses an old packet -> currentness rejection.
10. Difficult, limited, timed-out or inconclusive judged rows disappear -> denominator failure.
11. A green generic CI/package run substitutes for the support packet -> reject.
12. Reordered evidence preserves normalized identity; material rulings/evidence change it.

# Acceptance

- [ ] every ruling above has exact accepted evidence, deciding criterion, non-claims and change condition;
- [ ] compiled release payload, Cargo defaults and runtime activation are explicitly independent;
- [ ] preview/stronger support is an explicit per-surface/per-mode decision, not inferred from feature status;
- [ ] false-actionable and false-exposed results remain separate with complete denominators;
- [ ] unsupported/unqualified targets/channels/surfaces are omitted or named, never generalized;
- [ ] Go-less, disabled, unavailable, partial, failed and zero-subject states remain separately testable;
- [ ] optional versus required Go-toolchain behavior is explicit by capability;
- [ ] support/capability matrices and canonical docs can consume one versioned packet;
- [ ] #6230, #6240, #6243, #6246/#5553 as selected, source #1819 and public copy receive exact downstream obligations;
- [ ] no publication or external action occurs.

# Terminal deferrals allowed for a bounded preview

With explicit non-claims, the following may be deferred without blocking the minimum useful preview:

- #5549 third-party assertion families;
- #5554 toolchain enrichment;
- repository mode beyond an accepted #5765 limitation;
- auto-detection/default enablement;
- wheel/npm/editor/generated-CI/native-manager channels not selected for the release;
- verification-plan integration.

A deferred capability cannot remain in public copy, package metadata or selected channel rows.

## Invalidation

Parser/source-span/project/binding/activation/oracle/relation/output/corpus movement invalidates affected semantic rulings. Feature/build/payload/package/target movement invalidates affected availability/channel rulings. A successor packet is required; never edit exact identity fields in the accepted packet.

## Non-goals

No analyzer fix, parser swap, package build, default-feature edit, activation implementation, docs rewrite, registry publication, tag/release, package-manager submission, settings/protection change or stable-tier promotion by implication.

## Claim boundary

Closing #5556 states exactly what the accepted Go delivery supports, how it is activated, what ordinary Cargo installs contain, and where the selected evidence applies. It does not make unproved paths correct or publicly available.

issue.body:
Parent: #4493.
Depends on: #4631 and #4632.
Go distribution consumers: #6225/#6227/#6229, #6231/#6233/#6234/#6237/#6238, #6240/#6243, #6245/#6246 and accepted Go product paths under #5520.

## Outcome

Wire least-privilege CI routing and retained exact-subject handoff for package/native-payload changes, including the complete Go distribution dependency surface. Product, payload, package, fixture, copy and workflow changes trigger only the qualification needed to falsify their claims; docs-only changes do not silently rebuild native artifacts.

## Shared routing contract

- Derive or centrally register path groups for package adapters, native payload/build identity, consumer fixtures, output/contracts, quickstarts and generated workflows.
- Use read-only repository permissions. Qualification jobs receive no `id-token: write`, registry/release permission, secrets or publication capability.
- Build exact candidate artifacts once per selected generation and hand them between jobs with source/tree/version/target/feature/payload/package identity; never rebuild a different subject downstream.
- Retain bounded typed receipts/logs as Actions artifacts and feed the existing aggregate gate.
- Fail closed on missing artifact, stale receipt, insufficient permission, unexpected rebuild, ambient binary or incomplete route.
- Keep routing semantics and actual workflow triggers in parity; adding a path without a route or a route without an owned claim is a violation.

## Go route inventory

The accepted implementation must bind the actual landed paths, not these indicative names alone. At minimum classify and test:

### Product/semantic changes — require Go producer + installed semantic requalification

- `LanguageId::Go`, `lang-go`, routing/config/availability;
- Go parser/dependency/build-script/generated-C/helper/runtime inputs;
- Go project/package/build-context/source/binding/owner/test/activation/oracle/relation/limitation code;
- shared capability/witness/project/activation/completeness/miss schemas consumed by Go;
- Go output, SARIF, MCP/LSP/editor projection;
- Go fixture/corpus/expected-result/config files.

These paths trigger applicable product tests plus #6231 journeys/#6238 when they can move public semantic results.

### Build/payload/package changes — require exact artifact regeneration and package qualification

- workspace/Cargo feature/default/lock/toolchain and #6225 distribution-build contract;
- final payload/release-server/target/archive identity;
- Python Maturin and npm launcher/native package authoring/generation;
- native compatibility floors and any selected helper layout;
- package qualification schema/gate/harness.

These paths trigger #6227/#6229 and selected #6233/#6234/#6237/#4624/#4628/#6238 rows.

### Copy/quickstart changes — no native rebuild unless artifact claims moved

- Cargo/PyPI/npm metadata descriptions/keywords/classifiers;
- package READMEs/root installation docs/support/configuration/install-channel docs;
- version-specific snippets/link/output-copy fixtures.

Pure wording/links trigger #6240/#6243/#4629 product-copy/snippet checks. A feature/target/version/package-contents claim in the same diff escalates to artifact/package qualification.

### Generated installer/workflow changes

- native target/asset/checksum/extraction templates;
- generated workflow/SARIF/summary/artifact scripts and replay fixtures.

These trigger #6245/#6246 plus affected archive/Go output controls.

### Source-publication paths

Swarm qualification may produce artifacts/receipts for source handoff, but no swarm path receives publisher/OIDC permissions. Source-owned publication workflows remain out of this routing authority.

## Required controls

1. Remove one Go parser/dependency/generated path from routing -> route-coverage test fails.
2. Change `lang-go`/distribution features and trigger only docs checks -> fail.
3. Change package README prose with no artifact claim -> native build is correctly omitted while snippet/copy checks run.
4. Change metadata to claim a new target/feature -> artifact/package rows become required.
5. Change Go fixture expected output without product tests/installed semantic rows -> fail.
6. Change final payload after package jobs received it -> digest/currentness failure.
7. Downstream job rebuilds from source rather than consuming handed artifact -> fail exact-subject contract.
8. Missing artifact/receipt or zero required subjects -> aggregate failure.
9. Plant ambient ripr -> anti-ambient check fails if selected artifact is not used.
10. Add `id-token`, package/release write permission, secret dependency or publication step -> permission policy fails.
11. Equivalent path reordering does not change semantic route set; a new classified path does.
12. Existing Rust/Python/TypeScript routing remains accepted.

## Acceptance

- [ ] all landed Go semantic, parser/dependency, payload/package, fixture, copy and generated-workflow paths have one explicit least-privilege route;
- [ ] path changes select the minimum sufficient product/package/installed checks without hiding a required claim;
- [ ] docs-only changes avoid native rebuilds unless their claims require artifact verification;
- [ ] exact candidate artifacts/receipts are handed between jobs and remain visible in final #6238 evidence;
- [ ] missing/stale/wrong-subject/ambient/zero-subject states fail closed;
- [ ] a negative route-removal experiment proves the route inventory is load-bearing;
- [ ] workflow permissions remain read-only and publication-incapable;
- [ ] routing, workflow/file/non-Rust/generated policy and aggregate gate tests pass.

## Non-goals

No release orchestration, signing, tags, credentials, registry publication, branch-protection change, analyzer implementation or requirement that every optional package-manager channel run on every PR.

## Claim boundary

Completion proves CI selects and preserves the exact evidence needed for changed distribution/Go claims with least privilege. It does not qualify the artifacts itself or authorize publication.
